title: Falcon 9 rocket launches Dragon spacecraft for resupply mission
excerpt: The spacecraft and rocket launched from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on October 13 to head toward low Earth orbit.
bodyHtml:
A Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon spacecraft launched into the predawn sky on October 13 from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. According to NASA, the vehicles headed for low Earth orbit on NASA's 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission.

The flight chased the International Space Station, which entered the frame of a captured timelapse video almost 8 seconds in. The bright streak of the space station appeared heading down toward the horizon.

The first and second stages of the Falcon 9 separated as an exhaust plume grew and caught the light of the rising Sun. The visible sequence of first stage boost back, re-entry, and landing burns began around 20 seconds into the video.

The second stage followed the space station toward the distant horizon while the jellyfish plume continued to drift in the predawn sky. The first stage landed successfully at Landing Zone 40.
